question: Which logical processors are SMT siblings of each other, which share a cache, and in which processor group is each?
reason: the logical processor to core map (which logical processors are SMT siblings, which share a cache, which group each belongs to) is exposed by GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getlogicalprocessorinformationex), a native call this Windows PowerShell 5.1 script cannot make without compiling code at run time, which the read only posture excludes; no CIM class documents the per logical processor mapping. Win32_Processor gives the core and logical processor counts (processors source), and Microsoft documents that a system with fewer than 64 logical processors has the single group 0 (https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/processor-groups)

documented_paths.why_not_used: native call; needs code compiled at run time, which writes to the temp folder, both excluded by the read only posture
read by the processors source; it tells whether SMT is enabled (NumberOfCores less than NumberOfLogicalProcessors), not which logical processor pairs with which

follow_up: a later collector with a documented native read, or the trace itself, must establish the sibling map; until then "CPU 6 and its sibling" is not evidence
